title: What If Niagara Falls Ran Dry? Engineers Actually Did It

scenes.text: What if Niagara Falls ran dry? Engineers actually did it, for about five months.
In 1969 the Army Corps of Engineers wanted to study the rock beneath American Falls.
They dumped more than 28,000 tons of rock to build a dam 600 feet wide, sending the river to Horseshoe Falls.
Rockfalls in 1931 and 1954 had left boulders at the base, some ten stories high.
Crews drilled core samples and traced water with dye. They found the boulders were likely holding the falls up.
So the plan to remove them was dropped. The dam came down, and the river poured back over that night.

description:
What if Niagara Falls ran dry?
In 1969 engineers dammed the river for about five months to study American Falls, then let it flow again.
What should we run through next?
